summary: NVIDIA pairs exceptional growth (revenue +85.2% YoY, earnings +214.5% YoY, and roughly 8x annual revenue from $27.0B in 2023 to $215.9B in 2026) with extraordinary profitability (operating margin 65.6%, net margin 63.0%, ROE 114.3%). The balance sheet is strong, with $53.17B cash exceeding $12.81B total debt and a 3.44 current ratio, alongside robust cash generation (operating cash flow $125.65B, FCF $46.34B TTM). Valuation is mixed: rich on book value (P/B 26.33) and trailing earnings (P/E 31.43) but reasonable on a forward basis (P/E 16.69, PEG 0.63), with 59 analysts at strong_buy and a mean target of $298.93 (~41% above the $212.45 price). The main caveats are high volatility (beta 2.20) and stretched multiples; notably, no direct competitive/moat data is provided, so the durability of these returns cannot be judged from the evidence.

dimensions.rationale: Latest-quarter revenue grew 85.2% YoY (E11) and earnings grew 214.5% YoY (E12). The annual revenue trend shows roughly an 8x increase over three years: $27.0B (2023) → $60.9B (2024) → $130.5B (2025) → $215.9B (2026) (E28). Multiple direct, current data points agree on an exceptionally strong trajectory.

Margins are outstanding: gross margin 74.1% (E13), operating margin 65.6% (E14), and net profit margin 63.0% (E15). Return on equity is 114.3% (E16). These point-in-time figures are all directly cited and uniformly strong.

The company holds $53.17B in cash (E19) against just $12.81B total debt (E20), a net cash position of roughly $40B. The current ratio of 3.44 (E22) indicates strong short-term liquidity, and the reported debt/equity of 6.55 (E21) is low and consistent with debt well below cash.

Valuation is genuinely mixed: the price is rich on book value (P/B 26.33, E9) and trailing earnings (P/E 31.43, E7), but more reasonable on a forward basis (P/E 16.69, E8) and attractive relative to growth (PEG 0.63, E10). The mean analyst target of $298.93 (E3) implies ~41% upside from the $212.45 price (E2). The growth-adjusted and forward multiples tilt this positive, but the high P/B keeps confidence at medium.

Trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow is $125.65B (E18) and free cash flow is $46.34B (E17), both robustly positive. The ~$79B gap between operating and free cash flow implies heavy capital expenditure/investment, but cash generation is large and clearly positive on both measures.

The evidence contains only a descriptive business summary (E29) covering the Compute & Networking and Graphics segments and product lines, with no market-share figures, competitor comparison, pricing-power metrics, or switching-cost data. While the very high margins and ROE could indirectly suggest pricing power, there is no direct competitive evidence on which to base a moat rating, so this dimension is left as insufficient_data.

Sentiment is strongly favorable: the 52-week price change is +47.4% (E25), analyst consensus is strong_buy (E26) across 59 covering analysts (E27), and the mean target of $298.93 (E3) sits well above the $212.45 price (E2). The price is about 10% below its 52-week high of $236.54 (E4). The elevated beta of 2.20 (E24) flags high volatility as a caveat.

Concrete risk signals are present in the form of stretched valuation multiples — price/book of 26.33 (E9) and trailing P/E of 31.43 (E7) — and high volatility with a beta of 2.20 (E24); the stock also trades below its 52-week high of $236.54 (E4), leaving downside risk if the elevated growth decelerates. These are partly offset by the net-cash balance sheet and strong cash flow, so the rating is negative rather than strong_negative. The recent-news headlines (E30-E34) are vague or off-topic and were excluded as risk evidence.

key_risks: Stretched valuation multiples on book value (P/B 26.33, E9) and trailing earnings (P/E 31.43, E7) leave little margin for error if growth slows.
High volatility relative to the market (beta 2.20, E24), implying large drawdown potential.
Heavy capital intensity: free cash flow of $46.34B is far below operating cash flow of $125.65B (E17, E18), indicating large ongoing investment requirements.

Extremely high recent growth rates (revenue +85.2%, earnings +214.5%; E11, E12) on a now-large $215.9B revenue base (E28) may be difficult to sustain, and the price already sits ~10% off its 52-week high (E2, E4).
data_gaps: No competitive/moat data: market share, competitor comparison, pricing power, or switching costs are absent, preventing assessment of return durability.
No customer or revenue concentration data despite an AI-infrastructure business model.
No segment-level revenue or margin breakdown, only company-wide figures.
No historical margin or cash-flow trend — margins and cash flows are point-in-time only.
No share-count, dilution, or buyback information to gauge per-share effects of capital returns (only a 0.47% dividend yield, E23).
No quantification of geopolitical/export-control or supply-chain exposure, despite operations noted across China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong (E29).
No debt maturity schedule or interest-coverage detail beyond aggregate cash and debt balances.
